Left: A, C, E share no edge, so is_independent_set() returns True. Right: A, C, F, where the edge between C and F (shown in the accent color) joins two members, so is_independent_set() returns False." width="100%"} An independent set (also called a stable set) is a set of vertices in a graph where no two vertices are adjacent. This method validates whether the given nodes satisfy this property by looking at the neighbors of each node and returning `False` as soon as one of them is also in the set. Independent sets show up whenever edges represent conflicts: a set of jobs that can run at the same time, facilities that are far enough apart, or survey respondents with no direct ties to one another. Use this method to: - verify a candidate set built by hand or by an external tool - confirm the output of `maximal_independent_set()` or `maximum_independent_set()` - check one color class of a coloring (every color class must be independent) Edge direction is ignored: if the graph has `A -> B`, then `A` and `B` cannot both be in the set. Self-loops are ignored, so a node with a self-loop can still belong to an independent set. The empty set and any single node are always independent. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [nodes]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[int]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A list of integer node IDs to check. Labels are not accepted; use `get_id_from_label()` to convert them. Duplicate IDs are harmless. Every ID must exist in the graph, otherwise a `ValueError` is raised. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : `True` if the nodes form a valid independent set (no edges between them), `False` otherwise. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If any ID in `nodes=` is not a node in the graph. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} An independent set contains no adjacent vertices, so validation reduces to scanning the neighbors of each node in the set for another member: a single such edge witnesses invalidity. The cost is proportional to the total degree of the nodes in the set, so at most $O(V + E)$. Empty and singleton sets pass trivially. The dual property, that the *complement* of an independent set is a *vertex cover*, is what ties this validation to some of the most well-studied problems in combinatorial optimization. ## Examples {.doc-examples} On a path `A-B-C-D`, `A` and `C` are not directly connected, so they form a valid independent set: ::: {#fc60aad9 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_nodes(["A", "B", "C", "D"]) .add_edges([("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "D")]) ) a_id = graph.get_id_from_label("A") c_id = graph.get_id_from_label("C") # Returns True graph.is_independent_set([a_id, c_id]) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` True ``` ::: ::: Adding `D` breaks it, since `C` and `D` are adjacent: ::: {#e862fde2 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} d_id = graph.get_id_from_label("D") # Returns False graph.is_independent_set([a_id, c_id, d_id]) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` False ``` ::: ::: This is a handy way to confirm that a computed independent set is actually valid: ::: {#a87a61d1 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ec.Graph() graph.add_path_graph(10) mis = graph.maximal_independent_set(seed=23) # Returns True: maximal_independent_set() always produces a valid result graph.is_independent_set(mis) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` True ``` ::: :::
